title: Lint the raw hex-suffix pattern the opacity helpers cannot protect
body:
## Summary
withOpacity now handles var(), but 945 template literals still glue a suffix on directly and stay exposed to the same invalid-CSS bug.

## Description
A static count over src (excluding chart-colors and tests) finds 464 `${x}${OPACITY_n}` sites and 481 `${color}33`-style sites in 273 files. Any of them whose color is a var() still emits invalid CSS. Tonight's hand repairs were all this class. An ESLint rule banning the pattern, with an autofix to withOpacity, closes it.

## Flow
- add a no-restricted-syntax rule on template literals ending in an OPACITY token or two hex digits
- autofix to withOpacity
- migrate in batches per context

## Expected impact
The var()-suffix defect becomes impossible rather than repaired per site. Risk: large mechanical diff across 273 files.

## Evaluation
Claim: withOpacity now handles var(), but 945 template literals still glue a suffix on directly and stay exposed to the same invalid-CSS bug.
Before: 945 raw suffix sites in 273 files
After: 0 sites, lint-enforced
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: ESLint rule run over src reporting the remaining count, plus the combined vitest gate after the autofix

title: Judge verdict views colour 0-100 scores with the 1-5 qualityColor scale
body:
## Summary
JudgeVerdictsView feeds 0-100 scores to qualityColor, so nearly every verdict score renders muted.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/JudgeVerdictsView/index.tsx:90,98,128,160, VerdictDetailModal.tsx:47,56 and VerdictScoreTrend.tsx:79 pass a 0-100 value to qualityColor, whose domain is 1-5 and which returns var(--text-muted) above 5. Same defect as DimensionScoreBars, fixed tonight in 1 file inside this context. Line 90 passes a pass-rate percentage. A score of 3 of 100 reads amber.

## Flow
- replace with scoreBandToken(score).color
- pin one band case per view

## Expected impact
Verdict scores read by band like every other score surface. Risk: tests asserting the muted colour.

## Evaluation
Claim: JudgeVerdictsView feeds 0-100 scores to qualityColor, so nearly every verdict score renders muted.
Before: 7 call sites paint 0-100 scores muted
After: 0 sites
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Component test asserting the band colour for a 95 score in each of the 3 files

title: Modal stops trapping Tab and Escape once focus leaves the panel
body:
## Summary
The focus trap and Escape handler live on the panel, so they die when focus falls to the body.

## Description
src/components/ui/Modal.tsx handleKeyDown is bound with onKeyDown on the panel. If the focused control is removed or disabled, or the backdrop is clicked with closeOnBackdrop=false, focus moves to body and keydown never reaches the handler: Escape does nothing and Tab walks the page behind an aria-modal dialog. The `within` check in the handler shows the case was anticipated but it cannot run.

## Flow
- open a Modal with closeOnBackdrop=false
- click the backdrop
- press Escape: nothing; press Tab: focus enters the page behind

## Expected impact
Keyboard users cannot be stranded. Risk: a document-level listener must respect nested modals (ConfirmDialog inside Modal).

## Evaluation
Claim: The focus trap and Escape handler live on the panel, so they die when focus falls to the body.
Before: Escape and Tab inert with focus on body
After: both handled by a topmost-modal document listener
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Browser or jsdom test with focus on body and nested modals, asserting only the topmost closes

title: Range primitives set accentColor under appearance-none, where it has no effect
body:
## Summary
StyledSlider and RangeSlider pass accentColor to an appearance-none input, so the caller's accent never paints.

## Description
accent-color applies only to natively rendered controls. src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx sets appearance-none and a thumb with a border but no background, and src/components/ui/RangeSlider.tsx documents its thumb colour as derived from accent while also using appearance-none. .center-slider in globals.css is the working pattern.

## Flow
- render a StyledSlider with a non-default accent
- compare the thumb and track colour with the accent

## Expected impact
Slider accents match their module. Risk: visible restyle of 6 consumer files.

## Evaluation
Claim: StyledSlider and RangeSlider pass accentColor to an appearance-none input, so the caller's accent never paints.
Before: accent has no visible effect on the thumb (by CSS spec, not yet observed)
After: thumb painted from a CSS variable
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Browser screenshot of each slider with a non-default accent, before and after

title: statusToColor reports any unknown status as FAIL
body:
## Summary
An unrecognised widget status renders as a red FAIL rather than as unknown.

## Description
src/lib/chart-colors.ts statusToColor falls back to the error colour and the FAIL label for every status outside ok/warn/error. A new or misspelled status reads as a failure the system never measured.

## Flow
- pass a status outside the three known values
- the widget shows red FAIL

## Expected impact
Unknown reads as unknown. Risk: callers relying on the fallback; consumers need enumerating first.

## Evaluation
Claim: An unrecognised widget status renders as a red FAIL rather than as unknown.
Before: unknown status -> FAIL
After: unknown status -> neutral unknown
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Enumerate statusToColor callers and their status domains, then a unit test on the fallback

title: contrast helpers read a CSS variable as black without saying so
body:
## Summary
hexToRgb parses var() to NaN, which the bit shifts turn into black, so a contrast check returns a confident wrong ratio.

## Description
src/lib/contrast.ts:21-26 does parseInt then shifts; NaN >> 16 is 0, so var(--x) reads as #000000. A 4-digit #rgba is not expanded either. Any contrast assertion fed a token instead of a hex reports a number that was never measured.

## Flow
- contrastRatio(var(--x), #ffffff) returns 21

## Expected impact
A check that cannot measure says so. Risk: throwing could break tests that pass tokens today.

## Evaluation
Claim: hexToRgb parses var() to NaN, which the bit shifts turn into black, so a contrast check returns a confident wrong ratio.
Before: non-hex input -> ratio against black
After: non-hex input rejected explicitly
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Run the contrast tests with a throwing hexToRgb and list what breaks

title: withRoute returns raw exception text to the client
body:
## Summary
Every wrapped route sends error.message verbatim, which can carry filesystem paths and SQL text.

## Description
src/lib/api-utils.ts withRoute logs the error and also returns error.message in the 500 body. On this local tool the exposure is small, but the same text is rendered in UI banners, and a consumer reads paths and driver messages as product copy.

## Flow
- a route throws a SQLite error
- the client banner shows the raw driver message

## Expected impact
Decide which errors are safe to surface. Risk: many tests and banners rely on the message text.

## Evaluation
Claim: Every wrapped route sends error.message verbatim, which can carry filesystem paths and SQL text.
Before: raw message in every 500
After: allow-listed message, detail in logs
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Count tests and UI paths asserting on server error text before changing the contract

title: Modal uses z-50 while the Z_INDEX scale assigns modals 60
body:
## Summary
The modal shell ignores the shared z-index scale and ties with toasts.

## Description
src/components/ui/Modal.tsx renders the backdrop with z-50; src/lib/constants.ts defines Z_INDEX.toast 50 and Z_INDEX.modal 60. Paint order between a modal and a toast then depends on DOM order.

## Flow
- open a Modal while a toast is visible
- compare with the documented stacking order

## Expected impact
The scale means what it says. Risk: a deliberate toast-above-modal arrangement would invert.

## Evaluation
Claim: The modal shell ignores the shared z-index scale and ties with toasts.
Before: modal z 50 = toast z 50
After: modal z 60 per scale
Method: simulation
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Browser check of a toast shown over an open Modal, deciding which should win

title: Comments in the token layer state cuts the code no longer uses
body:
## Summary
ScoreRing documents a >=40 band and BORDER_HOVER documents 37%; the code uses 50 and 40%.

## Description
src/components/ui/ScoreRing.tsx scoreToStatusColor comment says >=40 orange while SCORE_BANDS cuts at 50. src/lib/chart-colors.ts BORDER_HOVER says 37% but aliases OPACITY_37, which is OPACITY_40. CLI_ANIM in src/lib/constants.ts also restates 0.12 and uses 0.2 beside DURATION.base 0.22.

## Flow
- correct the two comments
- derive CLI_ANIM.fast from DURATION.fast; decide whether medium should be base

## Expected impact
Docs match the values. CLI_ANIM.medium is a 20 ms visible change if aligned.

## Evaluation
Claim: ScoreRing documents a >=40 band and BORDER_HOVER documents 37%; the code uses 50 and 40%.
Before: 2 stale comments, 1 duplicated duration
After: 0
Method: probe
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: A source check of the comment values against SCORE_BANDS and the OPACITY aliases
